sections.content:
Introduction (history etc.)
Arithmetic (incl. Binary and hex number systems, floating points, logic operations, and mips stuff)
Performance of cpu
Logic gates, logic circuits, Boolean algebra
Single cycle pipeline
Multi cycle pipeline
Memory and cache

This isn't a very practical course per se, it's very theoretical. But it's fun, and you get to understand how computers works (kinda). Like you kind of get to see why programming languages behave the way they are as well. I was taking comp1023 the same semester and I'd say this course helped my understanding in object reference (deep copy vs copy and stuff like that) since i learnt how the computer memory works in this course. Also it helped my understanding of recursion.
sections.teaching:
The lecture teaching is a bit boring bc it's monotonous, but the content is interesting.

It was also a 3 hour long lecture so if you didn't catch the first half, you'd be cooked for the second half since everything builds on top of each other.

However, the tutorial session is very good, the TA is very helpful and is eager to answer every question you have regarding the course. The TA even respond to your emails at midnight.

Lab experiment 20%
Final Exam 45%

Midterm has more computation problems which im isnt a fan of cuz it's time consuming. I'd say practice more the calculation for midterm, like converting number to binary, to floating points and vice versa.

Oh yeah, also, no calculators for exams, which is a bit annoying but it was necessary (cuz if allow calculator then you can't really test on binary/hex number conversion)

sections.content:
Course Description
This is an introductory course in computer organization. The topics covered include instruction set architecture, assembly programming, computer arithmetic, computer performance evaluation, single-cycle processor design, multi-cycle pipelined processor design, memory system, and typical computer design flow. 

Topic:
L1: Introduction of Computers
L2: Arithmetic for Computers I
L3: MIPS Instruction Set Architecture
L4: Computer Arithmetic
L5: Computer Performance
L6: Review of Digital Logic Circuit
L7: Single-Cycle Processor Architecture
L8: Pipelined Multi-Cycle Processor Architecture
L9: Memory Architecture
sections.teaching: I took ELEC2350 with Professor Zhiyao Xie, and overall, it was a solid and enjoyable course for anyone interested in understanding how computers work under the hood.Professor Xie teaches really well. He explains complex concepts—like MIPS instructions, single-cycle and pipelined processors, arithmetic operations, and hazards—very clearly and step-by-step. The lectures are well-structured, with good examples and slides that make it easy to follow. Even if you’re new to computer architecture, his explanations help build a strong foundation without feeling overwhelming.
sections.grading:
Grading:
- Homework 1 & 2: 10% (5% each)
- Lab 1, 2, 3, 4: 20% (5% each, Attendance required)

- Final Exam: 45%
sections.workload: One of the best parts is the low workload. There are only four labs and two programming assignments, which are manageable and directly reinforce the lecture material. No heavy weekly homework or excessive projects, so it leaves plenty of time for other courses while still learning a lot.

sections.content:
very introductory course to computer hardware (MIPS structure).
IDK why they didn't teach RISC something more advance assembly code (maybe quite difficult to understand？)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Content:
I will rate the importance and explain the content between 10 Lectures
from LV1-5:

Lecture 1 Introduction of Computers (LV 1)
->teach the history and function of different component in PC(i.e. CPU/memory something like that, very trivial and no need to memorize them)
Lecture 2 Arithmetic for Computers - I (LV 3)
->binary/hexadecimal/decimal conversion .Two’s Complement Arithmetic etc...
should be no problem if you have ICT background

Lecture 3 Instructions and Programs (LV5)
->Oh, this part is super super super fundamental and important cuz you have to understand MIPS instructions(which will test in midterm and final) . Make sure you 100% really understand how to write R/I/J type instruction and MIPS Addressing Modes.
Like we have a given instructions : add $t1 , $t1，$zero
and we were examined to transform it into binary/hexadecimal/decimal instructions : 0x01204820

Lecture 4 Arithmetic for Computers - II (LV4)
->also a very important topic to know how machine can undergo Addition/Subtraction/Multiplication/Division
I knew some of you might hear about IEEE754 ,yes, in this lecture it will also teach how machine can display floating point number

Lecture 5 Computer Performance (LV2.5)
->you may wonder what factors of overall performance are hardware related? Like i9-13900K has a Max Turbo Frequency 5.80 GHz, but how's 5.8GHz come from????
In this chapter, you will know what are CPI /CPU clock rate/cycle etc...
shd be easy for those who are interested in building PC 

Lecture 6 Review of Digital Logic Circuit (LV3)
->A review from ELEC1100 Digital Logic Circuit part.
i.e. AND OR NOR XOR NAND...
above is combinational logic. Shd be fine if you took ELEC1100 . In this course, it also basically teach sequential logic (i.e. S-R latch ).That is super tedious and you have to pay 100% attention to know the concept of storing a bit from the latch.
Fortuity, both exam didn't include sequential logic(maybe will move on in ELEC3310?) . If one question examined this type of topic, i believes most of you will real GG and screw everything.

Lecture 7 Single-Cycle Processor Architecture (LV 5)
->After you learnt MIPS instructions, it's time to know the CPU architecture . In a very tiny CPU, basically, it has CU(control unit),ALU,PC(program counter),Instruction memory, Data memory and register. You will totally understand what's going on  in CPU when we execute an instruction .

Lecture 8 Pipelined Multi-Cycle Processor Architecture (LV 5)
To reducing waiting time ,we have to speedup the process of executing the instructions ,right? So we have multi-cycle processor and more advanced -> pipelined processor

However, in pipelined processor, we have several problems
1.structural hazard (clock dependent)
2.data hazard (wrong data)
3.control hazard (beq, j  failed)
This chapter will try to solve those problem.
Please use some time to understand the concept. This chapter is very very important and will examine in final exam 

Lecture 9 Memory Architecture (LV2)
Final boss. very briefly to introduce cache. And THIS IS THE MOST DISAPPOINTING that they didn't teach any content from memory. Look at COMP2611 ,they explained quite well on memory architecture. After taking this course i still have no idea on what's going on in memory architecture, especially in cache cuz they teach it very briefly. Now i still have a hundred of question mark on my brain!!!!! Bruh

sections.content:
The content taught are similar to that of previous semesters. You should be able to grasp the concepts as long as you have a basic understanding of pseudo programming and data flow in CPU. Lecture videos are uploaded weekly onto the "Lecture Notes and Recording" Section.

Lecture Topics:

L0 Course introduction
L1 Introduction
L2 Computer Arithmetic (binary, decimal, hex number systems, Concersion and overflow)
L3 Instruction Program (MIPS instructions)
L4 Arithmetics II (IEEE754)
L5 Computer performance (CPI, clock cycle)
L6 Single Cycle Processor
L7 Pipeline Processor (Multistage, Pipeline and Hazards)
sections.teaching:
Professor Xie explains the concept pretty well and utilises the drawing board for better understanding of the topics. Whether it'd be Arithmetics or Datapaths. The power points are easy to follow, not too crowdwd with word and uses diagrams appropriately as assistant.

He does not like people talking in his class. He will not hesitate to stop the teaching, actively call you out and ask you to be quiet. If you want to have a smooth lesson, text your friends or wait untill after class.

The IA Dr. Vivian Ho is very nice and would encourage you to be more active in tutorials. Do not hesitate to ask her some questions afterwards. YOu may also send her emails about your enquiries on the Course materials or book a session with her to discuss at her office.
sections.grading:
Homework 1& 2 : 10% (5% each)
Lab 1 - 4 : 20% (5% each)
Mid term:  25%
Finals: 45%

MIPS reference sheet is available for your peronal use and during exams. be sure to try memorize the format of each type of instructions. Homework and lab are easy to complete. Make sure you do understand the proceedures and data paths throughly. Remember to indicate which numbering system you are using in your answers (e.g 15, 0b1111, 0xF)
sections.workload:
With only 4 labs and 2 homeworks across the semester, the workload is quite light.Both homeworks have under 8 questions, each usually with 2 to 3 sub parts. The time for completetion is very sufficient. HW 1 was due near mid term, HW 2 is due end of semester.

There will be quizs in the labs for attendance and knowledge checking puposes. The password will only be revealed at the lab so be sure to attend them.

DrMIPS will be used for all labs and can be downloaded from the canvas page. In case your PC can't open DrMIPS, I recommend using a virtual barn provided by UST. Pre-lab materials like manual, answer sheet and code generator are available the weekend before your lab session. Most of them are recording the data and short questions, so could easily finish it beforehand

sections.content: The course content provides a solid foundation in understanding the basics of compiler writing. I found the material quite interesting and engaging. It offers a good mix of theoretical concepts and practical applications, which helps in grasping the essential elements of computer organization and design.
sections.teaching: The teaching quality is commendable. The instructor is very dedicated and passionate about the subject, which makes the classes enjoyable and informative. Their enthusiasm for the material encourages students to actively participate and engage with the content.
sections.grading: I didn't achieve a particularly high grade, ultimately receiving a B. This may be due to the fact that many students performed well in the course. Additionally, I left the final exam nearly an hour early to catch a flight, which likely impacted my performance.
sections.workload:
The workload for this course is relatively light compared to other classes. As long as you understand the lecture notes, assignments can typically be completed within an hour. Regarding the lab work, the first lab requires some critical thinking, but most of the subsequent labs mainly involve recording experimental data, making them easier to complete.
Overall, I enjoyed the course and found it to be a valuable learning experience.

sections.content:
I don't repeat the things that have already mentioned by others. Just a few notes:

- The content difficulty is moderate as a 2000-level course. Understanding is the most important thing.

- The contents before midterm (L0 - L5) are easier than the contents after midterm (L6 - L8). Not a lot but need time to digest.

- This semester L2 digital logic is added, which is actually approaching to COMP 2611 syllabus :).

For CPEG stduents, I would recommend you to take ELEC 2350 if you want a better grade, COMP 2611 if you want to learn more (and challenge yourself).

- Doing Exercises is essential. If you think the exercises offered by the teaching team are not enough, go to search some online, or even self-create some (for topics before midterm), then use online calculator to check your answers.
sections.teaching:
Prof. TU is good at researching, but he is not good at teaching.

For his teaching atitude, I can give him B+ ~ A- because I could see he was prepared (may not be well-prepared) for the lectures. Also, he was willing to stay after class for a long time to answer students' questions, or discuss some EE, processor topics outside the syllabus. Therefore, he has a pretty good teaching atitude in my opinion.

For his teaching pace, I give him a C+, because he taught quite slow (cannot even cover the lab topics before the labs were held). And I don't think it was easy for everyone to catch up what he wanted to say.

For his teaching skills, I give him a C+. His pronounciation was sometimes unclear and he often suddenly discussd irrelevant topics in class. I understand he might want to make his lectures not that boring, but...sorry to say, it didn't help.

Overall, I would say... he is passionate, but has a room of improvement. I believe that he can do better in the future. But for this semester, I can only give him an overall B-.

-----------------------------------

The I.A. Vivian taught very well. Attend her tutorials can DEFINITELY help you a lot. Her logic was clear and she prepared things well. Also, she was very patient to answer students' questions. I will give her teaching an A+.

So overall, I give a B+ in teaching.

sections.workload:
Light as a 2000-lv 4-credit course.

2 HWs with each less than 10 problems (ofc have some sub problems) over the semester.

The labs... were the same as previous semester, except Lab 1, just copying data from simulation software DrMIPs and answer short questions. The only challenge was that the lab3 and lab4 were held before the relevant topics were taught, so you might need to revise the preview the slides before the labs.

Midterm and Final contribute a significant part of workload (just like many UST courses), since midterm and final are the main differentiators of students. Just one recommendation, clear the concepts periodically throughout the semester. Don't think that you can digest all the concepts all in a few days before midterm and final unless you are a human CPU.

sections.content:
Content is similar to past offerings, with the difference being an extra lecture on digital logic.

L0: Course Info
L1: Introduction
L2: Digital Logic
L3: Computer Arithmetic (I)
L4: Instructions and Programs
L5: Computer Arithmetic (II)
L6: Computer Performance
L7: Single-Cycle Processor Architecture
L8: Pipelined Multi-cycle Processor Architecture
L9: Memory Architecture

For this semester, L9 (memory) was not included in the final.
The content is not very difficult, although they claim that this is "not an easy course like ELEC1100" (I got a better grade here than in 1100).

Apart from the recommended textbook, I used "D.M. Harris and S.L. Harris, Digital Design and Computer Architecture (2nd edition), Morgan Kaufmann, 2012" as well. I feel like the practice problems in this textbook are of higher quality and would prepare you better for the exams.
sections.teaching:
Prof Tu is probably very new to teaching, and hasn't been in full-English environments enough to speak English very fluently, but the teaching quality improved quite a lot over the semester.
At the start of the semester, he stuttered quite a lot and tried to extend everything on the slides. But as the semester progressed, the amount of stuttering dropped a lot, and he would skip the less important bits and emphasize more on the important content.
After class he will stick around a while to answer questions (can range from 10-30 mins), so you can clear up anything you didn't understand. On a side note, asking in putonghua would probably be more useful than in English.

Just for the teaching attitude and helpfulness to students, I would definitely give an A. But counting in the beginning of the semester results in B here.

sections.teaching:
Prof. XIE teaches this course for the first time, but it's generally great! He has a solid knowledge in this field and is willing and patient to answer students' questions. He explains all the knowledge in detail and spend about 20~30 min to review the content of the last class every time.  But for me, he sometimes goes into details too quickly for us to follow him. At first, I'm not sure that wheter it's because I missed sth so I failed to understand the progress, but after discussing with some of my fellow students, we found all of us didn't catch up quite well.

The TA Vivian is one of the best TA that I've ever met. She explains the knowledge points during tutorials and labs quite efficiently. Also she's such a kind person that she would email you once you've submitted a wrong hw file to the canvas！
sections.grading:
Since we don't have access to the canvas page anymore, I can only write this part with my poor memory.
2*hw(7%+8%) mean~85 mine~full
4~5labs(20% in total) mean~95 mine~full
midterm(20%) mean~60 mine:75.2 (about +1SD)
final(45%)mean ~67 mine:95.5
final grade:A+
It's quite a good grade course I think. The midterm was not difficult actually, but the time was too limited for me. Also, the concepts were kind of abstract to me and I didn't fully understand part of the knowledge before the midterm. However, after learning the part after midtermm, you can find many different parts of the course can be linked together, and it's much easier to understand. Also, because final has abundnat of time, and the questions are not tricky at all, it's easy to finish all the questions in time and get a satisfactory score.
sections.workload:
Light actually.
The lab is just copying some data from the simulation software. Actually I think making the lab more challenging and push us to think more about the content would be better for the understanding to this course.
And each hw has only around 5 questions, which can be e done in 2 hours~3 hours.
All the workload in this course comes from preparing for the exam.

Content:

L7 - Pipelined Multi-Cycle Processor Architecture

The content is very interesting & gives a good introduction to how a 5-stage MIPS processor works. This is explained in a fair amount of detail & can be quite overwhelming. I recommend attending the lectures as the lecture notes don't explain much. Later on, the multi-cycle and pipeline processors are explained & use many of the concepts from the single-cycle processor. Overall the content isn't very difficult to understand, but there is quite a lot of content & there are a lot of little things to pay attention to, i.e. if a specific calculation is signed, what addressing mode is used, etc.
sections.teaching:
The prof is new but very engaging & is happy to answer questions (don't ask stupid ones because he will call you out on it). He has a tendency to zoom through content only to take his time in the next lecture to go over the same content again, which allows you to figure out what you missed.

Vivian is an amazing TA; she explains things well during the tutorials and quickly replies to emails.
sections.grading: It's fair; Vivian was more lax on the first HW compared to the 2nd one, so a lot of people lost marks because they didn't include units i.e. 0X for hex & 0b for binary. Dont have access to the course page anymore so cant give any specific grades.
sections.workload: It's alright; 4 labs aren't hard but extremely tedious & time-consuming. 2 HW assignments are alright & a midterm and a final. For some reason, the midterm was a lot more difficult than the final, so try to get a good mark for the midterm to get ahead as the final mean was a lot higher than the midterm.

sections.content:
Course Learning Objectives
Objective 1: Identify key computer hardware and software components and computer technology trends
Objective 2: Examine core instruction set architecture and assembly programming method
Objective 3: Use computer arithmetic techniques to represent and process data in computers
Objective 4: Use a range of methods to evaluate computer performance
Objective 5: Use a standard computer system design flow to systematically develop single-cycle processor architectures including datapath and control for an instruction set
Objective 6: Systematically develop basic multi-cycle pipelined processor architectures for an instruction set and handle hazards
Objective 7: Classify memory hierarchies and use cache to handle temporal and spatial locality in programs

project 2(25%) is to create a simple game of guessing the coordinate of the hidden treasure. (arrays are not involved in this one. but instead you need to do a lot of looping. Trust me, looping in assembly code is a real pain in the ass)
I would've finished it in like a hour or two if I were to use python or C. but it almost took me 3 days to finish both project 1 and 2.

I got 90% in project, 100% in lab and around 75% in homework and I got an A-

HOMEWORK IS IMPORTANT. DO REALLY SPEND MORE TIME AND BE MORE CAREFUL WHEN DOING HOMEWORK.
sections.workload:
I would say the workload is quite ok?
you get like a week or two for each homework though they are time consuming.
THE REAL PROBLEM IS THE PROJECT.
both project have the same due date so BE SURE TO START EARLY! I almost couldn't finish as I started really late.
otherwise it is really fine.

sections.content:

sections.teaching:
The overall teaching is satisfactory. Professor Kursun delivered the lecture pretty well and always makes sure that people can keep up with this pace. Sadly this is his last semester at UST.

Maybe some students who are very familiar with all these before hand thin the teaching is a bit slow, but for me I think it's good as I'm new to all these.

sections.workload:
The workload is really low. The 2 projects and homework are not hard.
However, you should be careful in homework as it is easy to make mistakes, and they cost you quite some marks.
Try to make your code look neat for the 2 projects and write good comments.
Also, try to do the projects early as you already have the knowledge to finish them a month before the deadline. It would make your final period easier.

sections.content:

ch1: introduction
ch2: instructions and programs

sections.workload:
I think the workload is fine.
2 HWs are not that difficult if you can follow the lecture.
There is a task for each lab, so 3 tasks in total. They are not hard at all, most are copy and paste with 1-2 LQs.
Mt and final projects are the hardest. It took me the longest time to finish them. Both of them are coding by using MARS and Dr.MIPS to finish the task in the project description. ( To avoid cheating, the tasks given to us are not the same as each other.)

sections.content: This is an introductory course to computer organization. The topics covered include instruction set architecture, assembly programming, computer arithmetic, computer performance evaluation, single-cycle processor design, multi-cycle pipelined processor design, memory system, and typical computer design flow. Mainly about MIPS. No requirement for attendance.
sections.teaching: Prof.MAN's teaches quite well. He gives many examples to illustrate a concept and the explanation is very clear. And he will explain the logic circuits and flow step by step, which means there's no difficulty in following the lecture.

sections.grading:
HORRIBLE GRADING
The main reason I decided to write this after a whole semester was mainly because of this. Initially i wanted to give this course a chance, thinking that it was only me who fked up the proj and got a shit grade,  but judging from goop's reaction it seems that many people got c range in 2020 fall too so I wrote this review to warn whoever is planning to take this course: you might be better off taking COMP2611.
Originally, when I started taking this course, I was told that it only has hw (20%), midterm (30%)  and final (50%), but then one week before the midterm, the prof just suddenly decided that it was not fair to hold online exams (??????) and decide to change the grading to hw (50%) and a final project. Seriously WTF after i fked up all hws and you tell me this????? And i didnt even know what my proj scores are, and I just directly got a C in the end :)
sections.workload: The workload is fine, since I didnt put a lot of effort in this course, there are only a couple of homeworks and a final project (which looks something like a comp assignment), but since this course is new and prof likes to make last-minute arrangements, this might not be the case for other semesters. Supposedly this course should have a midterm and a final, but it was replaced by a project instead.
